evidence.note: Before coding, stated explicit phased plan: write model.py, copy to model_optimized.py as a checkpoint, run parity, then iterate — clear correctness-then-optimization ordering.

Parity established via per-component localization (prefix vs suffix, state vs action tokens) and end-to-end loss/sampling via benchmark before any optimization began — independently checkable done-conditions.
Explicitly froze model.py as correctness checkpoint and optimized only model_optimized.py; began optimization only after parity passed.
Optimization run as discrete scoped experiments (KV-cache, then torch.compile) with a /tmp backup of the working optimized file before the risky compile experiment, then reverted when it stalled.
Confirmed the shim continues exporting the optimized checkpoint, closing the final milestone.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor 5: it stated the implement→parity→freeze→optimize ordering upfront, respected the correctness checkpoint (even backing it up to /tmp before a risky experiment), kept the shim pointed at the optimized file, and treated optimization as a bounded sequence of discrete, scoped experiments with keep/revert decisions. It approaches anchor 8 through per-component parity localization and end-to-end parity gating, but falls short of a fully explicit milestone hierarchy: the parity checks emerged reactively during debugging rather than being enumerated as independently-checkable milestones, and there was no risk-ordering of hardest components or upfront planning of the ≤8 optimization experiments as a coherent search. This places it at a 7.
